correctness.rationale: The Finding's global cycle bound and interior sharpness witness are correct. The displacement F(x)-x is positive on the left by concavity and negative on the right by convexity, using the right extension at b only for the sign argument. Thus each primitive two-cycle has a unique smaller left coordinate x. With t=(b-x)/b, H(t)=0 is equivalent to the return equation exactly when y=1-(1-a)t^2>b. H'' is negative then positive with at most one zero on the nonnegative interval; H' has at most two zeros and Rolle bounds the number of roots even counting admissible endpoints. At the witness a>b, the four stated rational signs force three interior admissible roots. The three sign-changing roots are simple by degree four; the derivative relation to the multiplier classifies the two sinks and the repeller, and the implicit function theorem gives open persistence. Independent rational root and multiplier enclosures were computed in /workspace/branches/audit_witnesses.py. The wording of the proof's multiplier formula is too broad if read for all cycles: t=0 is possible exactly when c=b, giving (b,1); the positive smooth multiplier argument applies to interior witness cycles, not generally at this switch. This does not affect the stated witness or the global census. The failed disposition concerns coverage and value, not a counterexample to the Finding.
